msg: requirements crit. 2 (RL >= 26 dB at 25.0 MHz), as-routed L = 7.21 nH, C1 at its 1 pF low stop, C_port = 3.5 pF, R = 49.0 ohm (select-on-test lower limit). Measured 38.84 dB.
crit. 2 at R = 50.0 / C_port 3.5 pF. Measured 43.93 dB.
crit. 2 at R = 51.0 / C_port 3.5 pF. Measured 38.24 dB.
crit. 2 at the unselected catalogue +5% corner R = 52.5 / C_port 3.5 pF. Measured 31.78 dB.
crit. 2 at R = 49.0 / C_port 4.7 pF (the NOMINAL as-routed parasitic). Measured 36.84 dB.
crit. 2 at the nominal build R = 50.0 / C_port 4.7 pF. Measured 39.12 dB - this is the headline 'at the low stop it still measures 39.1 dB' number in README s3.
crit. 2 at R = 51.0 / C_port 4.7 pF (select-on-test upper limit). Measured 36.23 dB.
crit. 2 at R = 52.5 / C_port 4.7 pF. Measured 31.19 dB - the README's '31.2 dB at the +5 % resistance corner'. 5.19 dB of margin.
crit. 2 at R = 49.0 / C_port 6.0 pF (pessimistic end of the parasitic band). Measured 34.71 dB.
crit. 2 at R = 50.0 / C_port 6.0 pF. Measured 35.82 dB.
crit. 2 at R = 51.0 / C_port 6.0 pF. Measured 34.15 dB.

THE BINDING ASSERTION of this bench: crit. 2 at the worst of all 12 builds - catalogue +5% resistance AND the pessimistic 6.0 pF port parasitic. Measured 30.37 dB = 4.37 dB of margin. There is no combination of the delivered part tolerances and the parasitic uncertainty band that fails crit. 2.
crit. 3 (RL >= 20 dB over 22.5-27.5 MHz) at the SAME fixed trimmer setting - worst point in band, not re-optimised per frequency. R = 49.0 / 3.5 pF: 38.64 dB.
crit. 3 at the nominal build R = 50.0 / 4.7 pF: 38.29 dB.
crit. 3 at the worst of the 12 builds, R = 52.5 / 6.0 pF: 30.07 dB - 10.07 dB of margin on a 20 dB in-band spec.

MARGIN ASSERTION, not the spec: the worst build must stay above 29 dB, i.e. keep at least 3 dB over crit. 2. Measured 30.37 dB. A reading between 26 and 29 dB means the parasitic or the residual inductance moved, and the design should be re-examined even though the letter of the spec still passes.
same margin assertion in band: 30.07 dB.
band lower edge 22.5 MHz, worst build: 30.68 dB.

band upper edge 27.5 MHz, worst build: 30.07 dB. The upper edge is the worse of the two - with the trimmer over-correcting, rising frequency increases the shunt susceptance error faster than it increases X.

WRONG-VALUE TRIPWIRE 1 - this is the bound that would have caught review-verify V1. The nominal build must read 39.12 dB, NOT the 71.8 dB a correctly-nulled board reads and not the 43.9 dB a 3.5 pF parasitic gives. The old bench modelled C_port = 1.3 pF and L = 6.9 nH and measured 72.58 dB here, which is outside this window by 32 dB. Any future edit to cpad or lrt that is not re-derived from the as-routed geometry trips this.

WRONG-VALUE TRIPWIRE 2, same idea at the corner that actually binds: 31.19 dB. The perfect-null value at this corner is 32.17 dB (see tuning_authority.cir rl_ideal_r525), so the upper limit of 32.0 also catches a bench that has silently stopped clamping the trimmer at its low stop.

THE V1 FINDING, ASSERTED AS A NUMBER: an exact null of the as-routed 7.21 nH at R = 50 needs 2.883 pF of TOTAL shunt C, but C_port alone already supplies 4.7 pF - so the trimmer would have to contribute MINUS 1.817 pF. It cannot; the board sits below the trimmer's null window and C1 bottoms out. A positive reading here means the parasitic budget has been reverted to the stale 1.3 pF figure (which gives +1.583 pF).

the same conclusion at the OPTIMISTIC end of the parasitic band: even at 3.5 pF the required trimmer contribution is -0.617 pF, still negative. The 'C1 bottoms out' finding does not depend on the parasitic estimate being exactly 4.7 pF - it holds across the whole 3.5-6.0 pF uncertainty band.
and at the pessimistic end: -3.117 pF.
the total shunt C an exact null of 7.21 nH would need at R = 50: 2.883 pF. Closed form L/(R^2+(wL)^2). Independent of the parasitic split.
the as-routed residual as reactance at 25.0 MHz: 2*pi*25e6*7.21 nH = 1.1325 ohm. Sanity anchor for every other bench.
C1 is AT its 1 pF low stop in the nominal build - the bench computes the best setting and clamps it, it does not assume the stop. Measured exactly 1.000 pF.
at the low stop with C_port 3.5 pF too: 1.000 pF.
at the low stop with C_port 6.0 pF too: 1.000 pF.
at the low stop at the +5% resistance corner too: 1.000 pF. All 12 builds bottom out; the delivered 1-30 pF Johanson 5602 has upward-only authority on this board.
informational: 20 dB also holds over the whole swept 20-30 MHz, wider than the 22.5-27.5 MHz spec band. Nominal build 37.53 dB.

20-30 MHz at the worst build: 29.75 dB. The response is nearly flat because X = wL is only 1.13 ohm - this one-port's frequency dependence is negligible next to its resistance tolerance and its port capacitance.
